observation: Fresh main normalized each federated change independently and then filter(Boolean) silently removed malformed entries. A candidate containing one valid change plus one invalid op/path/content entry could therefore remain executable as a partial plan, even though the provider proposed a larger validation scope.
changes: Detect malformed entries across the supplied changes array before building the canonical change map.
Fail the entire mixed plan closed by clearing its executable changes, expose invalid_change_count, and record INVALID_CHANGE_ENTRY risk evidence instead of silently dropping only the bad rows.
Keep ambiguity, hierarchy-overlap, validation-budget, consensus, and ranking behavior unchanged for fully valid plans.

verification.pre_fix_source_contract_replay: EXPECTED FAIL: (Array.isArray(rawChanges)?rawChanges:[]).map(normalizeChange).filter(Boolean) erased malformed rows while preserving valid siblings.
verification.post_fix_source_contract_replay: PASS: any malformed row makes the mixed proposal non-executable while leaving valid alternative candidates eligible for selection.
verification.focused_regression_contract: tests/federated-change-shape-integrity.test.mjs proves a mixed valid+copy plan normalizes to zero changes with invalid_change_count=1 and that a valid competing candidate wins selection.

truth_boundary: This cycle does not invent a new change IR or migration strategy. It only prevents federated normalization from silently weakening a provider-authored change plan before existing downstream change-set invariants can see it.
